findings.location: allowlists.json kinds.Pod.upstreamFields rows 'spec.resources (pod-level requests/limits)', 'spec.affinity.(anti)podAffinity terms labelSelector.matchExpressions[+]', 'spec.topologySpreadConstraints[*].labelSelector.matchExpressions[+]', 'env[*].valueFrom.fieldRef.apiVersion; env[*].valueFrom.fileKeyRef.optional'; kinds.Pod.ALLOWED_FIXED and RULED_OUT_BY_MANIFEST; README 'Allowed differences per kind'; scripts/admission_semantics_v2.py check_manifest (POD_SPEC_FORBIDDEN) and final_object; upstream pkg/registry/core/pod/strategy.go:98-101 (PrepareForCreate), :909-951 (mutatePodAffinity, mutateTopologySpreadConstraints), pkg/api/pod/util.go:2253-2278 (DefaultPodLevelResources), pkg/features/kube_features.go:1965-1972 (PodLevelResources Beta on since 1.34, PodLevelResourcesFixDefaulting Beta on in 1.37)
findings.finding:
Three create-path deltas are listed as rows with a FIXED value, but none of them has a disposition. They are not in ALLOWED_FIXED or RULED_OUT_BY_MANIFEST, not in the README's allowed differences, not forbidden by check_manifest, and not produced by final_object. A2 admits them.
- Pod-level resource defaulting. PrepareForCreate calls DefaultPodLevelResources, which runs before validating admission with both gates on. It fills spec.resources.requests, limits and hugepage limits. Probe PG: a manifest with spec.resources {limits: {cpu: 1, memory: 1Gi}} passes check_manifest. final_object adds no requests. check_final admits the object with the upstream requests added.
- The matchLabelKeys and mismatchLabelKeys merge into affinity terms and topologySpreadConstraints label selectors. Probe PH: a manifest with a matchLabelKeys constraint passes check_manifest, and check_final admits the object with the merged matchExpressions.
- The env fieldRef.apiVersion and fileKeyRef.optional defaults. Probe PN: check_manifest passes, and final_object does not add apiVersion v1.
This is the same class as round-1 F1: a server change outside the disposition tables while A2 admits. It is rated MINOR, not MAJOR, because each delta is a deterministic function of the A1-admitted manifest and of fields A2 already pins. The labels are protected by A2-RESERVED, and container resources by MC34 plus the LimitRanger annotation. No cluster state or plugin configuration chooses these values. Still, A2 rule 1 ('every field ... is one of' the three dispositions) is not literally met. An implementer copying the disposition tables or final_object would under-predict the native object (W03 T03).
findings.requiredChange:
For each of the three deltas, either:
- add it to ALLOWED_FIXED with its deterministic value and model it in final_object; or
- rule it out with a new MC code: no pod-level spec.resources, and no matchLabelKeys or mismatchLabelKeys, or forbid affinity and topologySpreadConstraints outright.
Add manifest vectors, or end-to-end vectors whose finalObject carries the upstream delta. Make the README allowed-differences list match.

findings.location: allowlists.json constraintCoverage.DISABLED_GATE_FIELDS ('SIGNER_GUARANTEED: the signer refuses fields of feature gates the W02g profile pins off'); kinds.Pod.RULED_OUT_BY_MANIFEST 'fields of disabled feature gates': 'manifest content (W03 signer)'; scripts/admission_semantics_v2.py check_manifest, check_claim C25 ('the signed manifests met check_manifest at signing'); upstream pkg/api/pod/util.go:2127-2131 (dropDisabledSchedulingGroup), pkg/features/kube_features.go:1622-1625 (GenericWorkload Beta default false in 1.37)
findings.finding:
Round 2 makes disabled-gate fields a signer obligation, but check_manifest has no rule for them. The A2 claim's only signer evidence is manifestConstraintsMetAtSigning, which C25 defines as 'met check_manifest at signing'.
Probe PI: a positive Pod with spec.schedulingGroup passes check_manifest. That is a field of GenericWorkload, which is Beta and default false in 1.37. DropDisabledPodFields removes the field before A2, and check_final admits the object without it.
So a claim can carry every evidence key C25 requires while the persisted object lacks a signed field, and no code in the contract enforces the obligation. W02g pins the gate set (SC15), so the drop is deterministic. That makes this a model and evidence gap, not an A2 bypass driven by cluster state.

Yes.
- A1-A4 carry W01 §3.2.
- A1 now lists ACTIVE, scope, deadline, observed policy generation and the stamped armed action, with the durable consumption before the first byte.

check_claim supports the A2, A3 and A4 claims the text supports, now including C25 and C26. One gap: it accepts an A1 claim without scope, deadline or armed-action evidence (R2-F4).
questionAnswers.Q4:
The new expressions are valid CEL for the v1.37 VAP environment, by static reading only; nothing was compiled.
- request.userInfo.username: request has the type kubernetes.UserInfo with username StringType (admission/plugin/cel/compile.go:69-70, 85, 257).
- has(object.data), has(object.binaryData), has(object.metadata.labels) and has(v.image) are field selections on DynType (compile.go:254).
- object.data.size(), 'ca.crt' in object.data and annotations.all(k, k == ...) are standard map size, membership and the all macro over keys.
- !(name == ...) || (...) short-circuits for every other name.
Failures are closed: under failurePolicy Fail a runtime error denies.
check_final reads the CEL faithfully on reachable inputs and in rendered order:
- ConfigMap: PUBLISHER, then RESERVED and IMMUTABLE, both skipped only for the reserved name;
- Pod: RESERVED, ECHO, TOKEN, PULL-SECRETS, IMAGE-VOLUME, TOLERATIONS, PRIORITY, PLACEMENT, PULL-POLICY;
- Service: RESERVED, TYPE, ALLOCATION, DEFAULTS.
Absent fields and empty maps (omitempty) are handled equivalently: an empty data map is refused in both. Required dereferences, exact types and the address parse now match CEL.
The guard is unchanged and safe. The status subresource is not matched, and nothing the platform needs writes admission objects.
The ConfigMap policy no longer blocks the root-CA publisher, so no required controller is blocked.
